question: For the first part of her journey, Sunita traveled at a speed of 450 m/min and, for the rest of the journey, at a speed 1.4 times her initial speed. If Sunita traveled a total distance of 33.3 km in 1 hour, what was the distance that Sunita traveled at a lower speed?
solution:
**Given:**

Speed₁ = 450 meter/min

speed₂ = 1.4 × (speed₁)

The total distance traveled in one hour = 33.3 km

**Concept Used:**

Average speed = total distance/total time

**Calculation:**

Speed₁ = 450 m/min = 450 × 3/50 km/h = 27 km/ h

Speed₂ = 1.4 × (speed₁) = 1.4 × 27 = 37.8 km/h

Total distance traveled in 1 hour = 33.3 km

Let the distance travelled at two speeds be x and (33.3 – x) km

⇒ T₁ + T₂ = 1 hour

⇒ x/S₁ + (33.3 – x)/S₂ = 1

⇒ x/27 + (33.3 – x)/27×1.4 = 1

⇒ (33.3 – x)/ 27 × 1.4 = 1 – x/27

⇒ (33.3 – x)/1.4 = 27 – x

⇒ 33.3 – x = 27 × 1.4 – 1.4x

⇒ 0.4x = 27 × 1.4 – 33.3

⇒ x = (37.8 – 33.3)/0.4

⇒ x = 4.5/0.4 = 11.25 km

**∴ The distance traveled by Sunita at a lower speed is 11.25 km.**

Now,

Ratio of time = 4.5 : 6.3 = 5 : 7

⇒ (5 + 7) = 12 units = 60 min

⇒ 1 unit = 5 min

So 5 units = 25 min

So the distance was covered at a lower speed = 27 × (25/60) 

⇒ 45/4 = 11.25 km

**∴ The correct answer is 11.25 km.**
